🧠 Crypto News Brief: The Fed's first rate hike since 2023 failed to break crypto: bitcoin held above $76K and privacy coins surged, while the Clarity Act's Senate collapse kept ETF money heading for the exits. 🏦 Fed Hikes Rates for the First Time Since 2023 The Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a 3.75%–4.00% range, its first increase since July 2023. Stocks slid after Kevin Warsh's post-decision press conference while bitcoin held steady, and Goldman Sachs now expects another quarter-point hike in October. Read full story 📉 Bitcoin ETFs Bleed $450M After Clarity Act Collapse U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs recorded about $450 million in net outflows, the largest since June, after the Senate failed to advance the Clarity Act market-structure bill. Tokens most exposed to regulatory risk took the sharpest hit. More details 🚨 Revolut Hackers Demand $3M Ransom in Monero A hacking group targeting Revolut is demanding $3 million in Monero and threatening to sell customer data if the fintech doesn't pay within 24 hours. The attackers say they focused on customers with large crypto holdings. Read more 🚀 Zcash Soars 23% as Bitcoin Shrugs Off the Fed ZEC rallied 23% as bitcoin moved back above $76,000 and major tokens gained despite the hike, helped by Fed projections signaling only limited further tightening. Paradigm's Matt Huang described Zcash as a privacy complement to bitcoin. See details 🧾 House Tax Panel Advances Crypto Tax Relief Bill The House Ways and Means Committee advanced the Digital Asset Tax Certainty Act, which aims to simplify taxes on everyday crypto use. The vote gives the industry a partial win after the Clarity Act defeat, though President Trump's crypto ties drew pushback. Get the details 🏛️ Deutsche Bank Nears Institutional Crypto Custody Launch Deutsche Bank is close to rolling out crypto custody for institutional clients. The service will launch with a limited set of assets, including bitcoin, ether and the USDC and EURC stablecoins. Full report ⚖️ Celsius Sues BitMEX for $495M Over 2020 Liquidations The Celsius bankruptcy estate filed a $495 million lawsuit against BitMEX, seeking to recover 6,360 BTC lost to liquidations during the 2020 Covid crash. The leveraged long position sits uneasily with the delta-neutral strategy Celsius once marketed. Read the story

79255.body:
Adrian's DeFi Insights 

Автор: Adrian Pape


Автор: Adrian Pape

Прочитати на LinkedIn

Hey, it's Adrian! Two days, two punches out of Washington. Ouch. On Tuesday the Senate failed to even start debate on the CLARITY Act. On Wednesday the Fed raised rates for the first time since 2023. Bitcoin took both and is still at $76k as I write. For a week like this, this is a real sign of strength. Underneath the price, something did change though. The new money that carried Bitcoin more than 30% off the June low has stopped buying and the ETFs lost over $1 billion in seven sessions. Though the selling pressure is showing up in altcoins first. I still think the cycle bottom is in. The next few weeks just look more like a correction than a breakout. Let’s get into the broader picture and how to set up for the coming week: ️ ⚡ On today's Episode: 📈 Market Update – The Senate blocked the CLARITY Act 49 to 50 and the Fed hiked to 3.75%-4% the next day, with the 10-year near 5% and Brent above $100. Crypto regulation is now realistically a 2027 story. 🔊 Market Pulse – Bitcoin slipped below its $76k-$82k range and its Bull Score fell from 80 to 60 in a week. ETFs lost $1.05 billion in seven sessions and the Coinbase Premium turned negative, while altcoin deposits on Binance nearly quadrupled since July. 🐂 Alpha Insights – Bitcoin entered my first $75.7k–$74.3k buy tranche. I’m still building the position gradually, while keeping leverage controlled and a liquidation price around $30k because a deeper correction remains possible. Start with Washington, because both hits came from there this week. On Tuesday the Senate voted on whether to open debate on the CLARITY Act, the bill that would finally decide which agency regulates which crypto assets. It needed 60 votes and got 49. The crypto rules themselves were mostly agreed. It fell over ethics: Democrats wanted rules for officials holding crypto that would actually cover the president and his family. Zero Democrats voted yes. The motion to reconsider is still on the table, so technically it isn’t dead. Realistically, with the midterms in November the next window is after the election or 2027. Bitcoin dropped about 4% to $76k around the vote and over half a billion dollars in long positions got liquidated. → Nothing about the rules crypto works under today changed on Tuesday. The timeline did. US banks and big funds that wanted clear rules before putting serious money in now keep waiting, and t
